To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a simple, straightforward implementation of transactions on NVR-AM imposes unnecessary constraints that limit performance; (2) these constraints can be removed using a variety of techniques including deferring commit until locks are released and deferring log record creation until the transaction commits; (3) we present a comprehensive evaluation of two different transaction designs across three different NVRAM programming interface, demonstrating up to a 2.5X speedup over the straightforward implementation.

(1) the performance of NVRAM transactions can be improved by removing unnecessary constraints; (2) this can be achieved through a variety of optimizations, including deferring commit until locks are released; (3) the performance of transactions is strongly dependent on the NVRAM programming interface used; (4) the performance of transaction systems using NVRAM programming can be up to 2x faster than those that do not use these interfaces.
(1) the design of a transactional memory system has a significant effect on performance and (2) deferring commit until locks are released can improve performance.
